candidateDecisions.label: Health technology, data and responsible innovation
Public health, prevention and healthy environments

analysis: The closest curriculum builds from anatomy, molecular biology, physiology and biochemistry to infection, drug action, disease and clinical psychology, with population and social context. Sociology moves earlier and molecular pathology follows physiology and biochemistry. The technology option gives actual grounding in Python, modelling, relational databases, neural networks, vision, robot motion and ethics. Linear algebra is moved before robotics. These methods have health applications but are not a dedicated clinical technology or diagnostic sequence. The public-health option combines epidemiology, health inequalities, research design and public economics with public argument and justice. The environmental justice course replaces unavailable spring Behavioral Economics, adds case-based study of unequal environmental burdens and complements sustainability governance. Introductory sociology is brought ahead of qualitative methods and modern sociology. The description-only database, perception and environmental justice courses have substantive roles in their respective options. Professional placements, the full human and animal comparison and the Societal Challenge remain distinct. The grouping was replaced by individual course rows, with partial pairings only where the sources support shared content. No career or clinical qualification is inferred.

alignment.rationale: Both study normal physiological regulation, including homeostasis. Utrecht also examines disruptions to that balance.
Both study anatomy and organ systems. Utrecht compares development and structure across species.
Both study drug action, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Utrecht considers treatment across patient groups.
Both address microbes and infectious disease. UCR also develops the mechanisms of immune defence.
Both examine organ-system disease. Utrecht applies clinical reasoning to human and animal cases.
Both examine cells, signalling and molecular processes. Utrecht applies these to human and animal health.
Both examine ageing and later life. UCR focuses on psychological development across the lifespan.
Both examine mental health and behaviour. Utrecht integrates medical, pharmaceutical and veterinary perspectives.
Both use data and statistical inference to investigate empirical questions. The applications and software differ.
Utrecht studies early human and animal development in a dedicated course.
